# Synthetic side-scan sonar surveys (XTF)

**Synthetic data**, generated by `ai/tools/generate_xtf.py`: a physically based simulation, not real survey recordings.
Use it to exercise the XTF path end to end (upload → waterfall → detection → geotag → map) and to measure
detection / geotag accuracy against a known answer key.

| Survey | Track | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `synthetic_wreck_site.xtf` | straight, 300 m, heading 58° | 46 m shipwreck with superstructure and debris field (8 pieces), one mine-like cylinder, 6 natural rock outcrops |
| `synthetic_mine_like_objects.xtf` | curved (95° → 70°), 300 m | 6 cylinders (mine-like / pipe sections), 2 shipping containers, a pipeline crossing both channels, sand ripples, 6 heave dropouts |
| `synthetic_rocky_seabed_negatives.xtf` | straight, 300 m, heading 210° | natural terrain only: 14 rock outcrops, 3 ridges, strong ripples. **Every detection here is a false positive** |

Sonar: 2 channels (port / starboard), 450 kHz, 50–60 m slant range, 1000 uint16 samples per side, 10 pings/s at 1.5 m/s,
towfish ~12 m above the seabed with heave. Survey area: off Chennai, Bay of Bengal (WGS-84).

## Files per survey
* `<name>.xtf`: the log. Ping headers carry sensor lat/lon (NavUnits = lat/lon), heading, altitude, speed, heave, time, slant range.
* `<name>_groundtruth.json`: every placed object: kind, expected detector class (`null` for natural features), lat/lon,
  ping index, side, ground range, length × width × height, orientation; plus the dropout pings.
* `<name>_nav.csv`: per-ping navigation (`ping, time_utc, latitude, longitude, heading, altitude`).
* `<name>_preview.png`: the waterfall exactly as the AI service reads the XTF (port | starboard, half size), for a quick look.
* `synthetic_evaluation.json`: latest scores of the AI pipeline on these surveys (`ai/tools/evaluate_synthetic.py`).

## What the simulation models
Slant-range geometry (ground range = √(r² − h²)), water column and first-bottom return, grazing-angle falloff with imperfect
TVG, sediment patches / sand ripples / grain, objects as height fields, **acoustic shadows by ray casting** from the towfish,
brighter faces towards the sonar, Rayleigh-like speckle, and ping dropouts from heave.
Not modelled: multipath, surface returns, towfish yaw/roll distortion, variable sound speed, absorption, beam pattern.

## How to use
* **App**: AI Detection tab → *Load Image(s) / XTF* → pick an `.xtf` → *Predict*. It is georeferenced automatically from the ping headers.
* **API**: `curl -F file=@data/synthetic_wreck_site.xtf http://localhost:5000/api/scans`
* **Regenerate / evaluate** (from `ai/`):
  ```bash
  .venv/Scripts/python tools/generate_xtf.py
  .venv/Scripts/python tools/evaluate_synthetic.py
  ```

## Current results (detector + segmenter, default settings)
| Survey | Man-made found | Right class | False positives | Geotag error (mean / max) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| wreck site | 3 / 11 (wreck + cylinder; small debris missed) | 2 / 3 | 4 | 2.9 / 6.7 m |
| mine-like objects | 8 / 8 | 0 / 8 (all called *shipwreck*) | 2 | 1.8 / 8.5 m |
| rocky seabed (negatives) | n/a | n/a | 8 (rocks called *shipwreck*) | n/a |

Localisation and geotagging work; classification on native side-scan strips is biased to *shipwreck*, because the only strip-format
training data (AI4Shipwrecks) is wreck-only, and shadow-casting rocks pass the false-positive filter.
